note: The project palette: Waldgeist, adopted for now. Every pixel of committed
ship art must be one of these colors: tools/shiplib.py verify() fails the
build on anything else, so a color cannot drift in unnoticed.
Colors live here rather than in the generators (CLAUDE.md 5.4), and the role
maps below live here too, because which palette entry plays 'hull plate' is
exactly the kind of thing a designer retunes. The generators name roles, not
The painting vocabulary still comes from the author's own sheets in
docs/examples/ship-art: R1-Starship-A for the frigate (blue on blue plate
bevels, silver rivets, dashed red machinery) and R6-Starship-A for the
raider (near black hull, purple panel work, dithered grilles, warm plumes).
This file changes what those shapes are painted in, not what they are.
ui_note: The interface skin. Two kinds of colour, and both answer to this file.
The CHASSIS is committed art: plates, bezels and the font atlas are written
as .png by tools/gen_ui_plates.py, and every pixel of them is an entry from
'colors' above, verbatim. The GLASS is light rather than paint: the readouts
a Control draws at runtime. Those need to sit brighter than any Waldgeist
entry does, because a lit instrument emits rather than reflects, so they
live in 'ui_colors' as their own named set. Each is a Waldgeist hue lifted
toward emission and its base is named beside it:
phos_hi phos phos_lo phos_faint   from green
shield_hi shield                  from teal
gold_hi                           from gold
blue_hi                           from blue_light
wine_hi rose_hi                   from wine
alert alert_hi                    from clay
They are deliberately NOT in 'colors', because tools/shiplib.py verify()
checks ship art against that block and an emissive must never be paintable
onto a hull. Ship art stays strictly Waldgeist; only lit UI may use these.
A SKIN BELONGS TO A FACTION, not to the build. ui_factions below says which
skin each side's deck wears, and a ship's hull says which side built it, so
the console a player is looking at is the console their own navy fits. The
Federation flies steel and the Kthaari fly verdant. ui_default_faction is
what the interface wears outside a battle, where no ship has named a side.
TO CHANGE A DECK, edit ui_factions below and run scripts/gen-skin.sh. That
repaints the plate textures and rewrites the theme for every faction named
there, both of which are build products of this file. Nothing else in the
project names a colour: the generators ask for roles like 'face' and
'accent', src/ui/palette.gd reads the lit map, and the theme is generated
rather than hand edited. This is what CLAUDE.md 3.1 means by a palette swap
being a one file change.
Each skin gives the same two role maps. 'chassis' is what the plate painter
asks for and must name entries from 'colors'. 'lit' is what palette.gd asks
for and may name either pool. A skin no faction names is simply not built.

verdant.note: The Kthaari deck: green phosphor on oxidised bronze.

steel.note: The Federation deck: blue readouts on gunmetal.

rose.note: Unassigned. No faction names it, so gen-skin.sh does not build it. Kept because a third navy will want a deck, and because its face and its panel are the same entry, which is a good reminder that a role map can be internally valid and still lose every panel frame.

cruiser._note: Federation heavy cruiser, the Wayfarer. Same marks as the frigate: docs/12 puts empire in proportion, not in colour.

ironhold._note: Battlecruiser on the cruiser hull. Colder plate and gold trim so it is not a big Wayfarer.

talon._note: Kthaari escort on the raider hull. Duller than the Bloodletter: the pair should read as a raider and its screen.

fx_note: Colour ramps for the effect sprite sheets, hottest entry first. A ramp is named here rather than written into a generator so that a palette swap stays a one file change (CLAUDE.md 3.1). Entries resolve against colors and ui_colors together, because the hot end of a fire is the same orange every critical readout in the interface already wears, and naming a second one would be inventing a colour.
ramps_note: Lookup ramps for the sky shader, baked to assets/textures/sky_ramps.png by
tools/gen_ramps.py. The shader never blends two colors together: it picks a
step from a ramp, so every pixel it draws is a palette entry and the sky
bands the way hand painted pixel art does.
One row per ramp, all the same length. Repeat a color to widen its band:
the four blacks at the head of each nebula ramp are what keeps most of the
sky empty so the ships stay readable on top of it.
star_dim is indexed by the same value as star, so a star's faint outer
step is a darker shade of its own color rather than a generic gray.

worlds._note: Colours for the pixel planet shaders vendored from Deep-Fold (docs/14). Each entry is the ordered list that world type's set_colors expects, and the vendored script decides where the slices fall. The shaders never blend: every pixel they emit is exactly one of these, dithered against its neighbour, so a world is made of palette entries and nothing else (CLAUDE.md 3.1). Within each band the order is lit side first, shadow last.
